THE SCOPE LIMIT, first, because it changes what you may claim. I profiled
`hornvale lab run studies/the-census.study.json`. The 1366.487 s figure the
alarm reads is NOT that — `scripts/census-run.sh:220` times
`HV_CENSUS=1 bash scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh`, which runs the census
study AND census-of-the-meeting AND every other generator. So this profile
covers roughly 744 of those 1366 seconds: the largest single component, and
the only one whose cost scales with world count, but not the whole row.

THE FINDING: THERE IS NO HOTSPOT.

    flat self-time, top symbol:
      4.71%  hornvale_kernel::noise::Fbm::sample
               -- 2.41% via hornvale_terrain::crust::sphere_fbm01
                          -- 1.86% GeneratedTerrain::cave_at
               -- 1.38% via plates::assign_plates / globe::generate

The hottest single function in the run is under 5% of self time, and it is the
noise field — the irreducible cost of deriving a world. Nothing above it. A
regression of the kind this alarm exists to catch (O(n^2) creeping in, entering
as a yellow run long before it is an obvious one) would show as a concentrated
peak, and there is none.

THE STRUCTURE, for your row's prose:

    82.83%  hornvale_lab::runner::build_row          (inclusive)
      49.61%  Vec::from_iter -> metrics::Extractor::apply
        13.65%  OnceCell::try_init -> lot::context::assemble_from (12.26%)
          5.65%  worldgen::demography_report_from_*

Read plainly: the census spends its time extracting metrics over worlds, and
about an eighth of that inside the lazily-initialised lot context. That is the
shape of "more metrics x more worlds", not of a scaling defect.

WHAT I THINK YOUR ROW CAN HONESTLY SAY: profiled, flat, no hotspot above 4.71%
self time, cost distributed across metric extraction as expected for the
surface size — with the scope caveat stated, because a reader who assumes it
covered all 1366 s will draw a stronger conclusion than the evidence carries.
That would be the FIRST row in census-yellow-log.tsv grounded in a profile
rather than in ledger arithmetic; the five above it all reason from
docs/timings.md by analogy.

AND THE THING WORTH MORE THAN YOUR ROW. Your overage is 3.5%. Byte-identical
censuses measured 1364.038 s and 1398.403 s tonight -- a 34 s spread on work
producing identical goldens. The ALARM is 1320, derived (census_duration.rs:252)
from n=1 at 1278.160 s with 42 s of headroom, set 2026-09-06. EVERY census since
has exceeded it: 1364, 1366, 1398, 1412, 1434, 1443. Six consecutive. An alarm
that fires every time is a toll, not an alarm, and it is why the rows above
yours all argue "within noise" -- they are describing a mis-set bar, not being
lazy. Re-deriving it from the current distribution is a better use of someone's
time than any individual row, and your null is the evidence for it.
